runs.text: por onde deſabafe, & vapore a cabeça.

lines.note: Continues the preceding page’s explanation of an outlet through which the head can release heat or vapour. The opening por belongs to the running gloss, not to a new entry.

runs.text: Guia que leua polla mao ao cego.

lines.note: Tefiqi is a guide who leads a blind person by the hand, matching te-hiki. The printed mao is retained without supplying a tilde.

runs.text: Treslado, ou modelo da letra. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Tefon denotes a model of handwriting or an exemplar. Treslado and modelo da letra give the literal sense before the figurative extension below.
Tefonni naru means becoming an example for others. The Portuguese per met. introduces this figurative application of the preceding handwriting model.
Completes Ser exemplo pera outros: to serve as an example for others. The scan shows exemplo as one word, without the OCR’s internal space.
Tegai is taming or domesticating an animal. Ne- begins the divided Neco in the example, while the nasal abbreviation in amãſar is preserved as printed.

runs.text: co, inu, tori nadouo tegaini ſuru.

lines.note: Neco, inu, tori nado wo tegai ni suru describes domesticating cats, dogs, birds, and the like. The Portuguese Amẽſar has a weak but retained nasal abbreviation rather than a silently regularized modern spelling.
Completes the taming example with domesticar gatos, cães, paßaros: domesticating cats, dogs, and birds. The historic spelling and long-s conventions remain occurrence-specific.
Tegamaxij characterizes a person restless or fidgety with the hands. Its Japanese te- element agrees with the hands specified in the continuation.
Mãos completes the description of fidgety hands. The upright X. is the dictionary’s regional usage label rather than part of the italic gloss.

runs.text: Certo vaſo, ou boceta em que metẽ

lines.note: Tegame names a vessel or small box holding powdered tea. The damaged initial syllable is Te-, supported by the visible e and this alphabetical context, rather than OCR To-.
Cha moido completes the vessel’s contents as powdered tea. Cha is a Japanese term embedded in the Portuguese explanation and is retained for optional whole-word typeface review.

Tegara is a distinguished accomplishment or feat. The worn Portuguese façanha is clarified by the fully readable plural façanhas on the next line; the printed Te fragment begins the divided Japanese example. The single ſ in aſinalada is left unchanged.
Tegara wo suru, alternatively arawasu, means performing or displaying feats. Garauo completes the preceding Te; the Portuguese Fazer façanhas directly confirms that sense.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Obra prima de mãos. Vt,

lines.note: The next sense is fine workmanship. Tega- begins tegara wo tsukusu, and the visible initial T corrects OCR Iega-.
Rauo completes tegara wo tsukusu, exerting one’s skill to the utmost. Esmerar-se em fazer alguma begins the explanation of striving to make something well.
Obra bem feita completes the workmanship example: a well-made piece of work. This short continuation closes tegara before the following personal designation.

runs.text: Homẽ que faz façanhas na guerra.

lines.note: Tegaraxa is a person who performs feats in war. The scan supports the abbreviated Homẽ and façanhas rather than the OCR’s malformed Homãẽ and fuçanhas.

runs.text: Destro na arte de eſgrima, ou em

lines.note: Tegaraxi means skilled in swordsmanship or another manual art. The worn headword agrees with the te-gara family above; Destro and arte correct separate OCR letter confusions.
Completes the skilled-person gloss with some other work of the hands. The entry is not restricted to military accomplishment.

runs.text: Diligente, & ligeiro de mãos, ou no

lines.note: Tegarui describes someone diligent and nimble with the hands. The Portuguese also extends the description to bodily movement in the continuation.
Andar and meneo complete the description of nimbleness in walking and movement. Preserve the historical form meneo rather than supplying a modern equivalent.
Tegaſa is an eruption or itch affecting the hands, glossed Sarna das mãos. The separate upright X. marks restricted regional usage.

This second Tegaſa, alternatively tegaſana, concerns a person surpassing another. The following line specifies the respects in which that superiority applies; it is distinct from the skin condition above. Peſoa retains its single visible long ſ, without supplying a second s from the modern spelling.
The comparison concerns income, power, and strength. Renda is the visible noun, correcting OCR tenda, and completes the divided outra.

runs.text: Aſas de panella, ou de outra couſa

lines.note: Tegata first names the handles of a cooking pot or similar object. Aſas is the ordinary Portuguese handle sense, rather than anatomical wings in this context.

runs.text: ſemelhante. ¶ Item, Hũs circulos de ferro

lines.note: After closing the general handle definition, Item introduces iron rings used for grasping a copper pot. Hũs is the printed abbreviated plural, left unexpanded.

runs.text: com que aferrão na panella de cobre, & a-

lines.note: The iron rings provide a grip on a copper pot. The trailing a- continues the clause about moving or handling it, and its physical terminal mark is retained.
Completes the clause about moving the pot with its gripping rings. Enlargement supports meneão, with a small worn e rather than the OCR’s c; the historical inflected form is preserved.
The second Tegata is the bow or pommel of a saddle, expressed by Arção da ſella. It is a separate noun entry despite the repeated headword.

runs.text: Couſa forte, teſa, & ſegura, que não

lines.note: Tegatai means strong, firm, and secure, applied to something hard to overcome. The headword’s damaged vowel is e, as confirmed by its repeated example below.

runs.text: ſe pode render facilmente, como fortaleza,

lines.note: Completes the negative clause: it cannot easily be overcome or made to surrender, a fortress being the example. This is the physical-strength sense of tegatai.
Tegatai hito applies the preceding adjective to a firm and steadfast person. The Portuguese desta laya is divided at the printed la- across the line end.
Completes the human application: a person of this sort, strong and constant. The wording concerns reliability and firmness as well as physical strength.
Tegataſa and Tegatǒ are the noun and adverbial forms accompanying tegatai. The visibly downward-pointing accent in Tegatǒ is retained.

runs.text: Hũa taboa furada em que metem as

lines.note: Tegaxe is a pierced wooden board into which an offender’s hands are inserted. The definition describes a form of restraint, with its effect continued below.

runs.text: mãos dalgum mal feitor, & lhe ficão ſujugadas.

lines.note: The offender’s hands remain restrained in the board. Mal feitor is visibly spaced, and ſujugadas is preserved without inserting a modernizing b.

runs.text: O fazerſe inimigo, ou tredo. Vt,

lines.note: Tegaye denotes becoming hostile or disloyal. The initial is a worn T, supported by the repeated Tegayeuo below, rather than the OCR’s F.
Tegaye wo suru repeats the act of changing to the hostile or treacherous side. The visible long ſ in ſuru corrects OCR turu; Idem refers to the same preceding explanation.
Tegui, alternatively ximegui, is a short wooden piece used in tightening a cord. The alternate name fits shimegi; the scan supports ximegui and paoſinho rather than the OCR’s xumegui and paoſiaho.

runs.text: q̃ embarulhão a corda pera apertar muito o ve-

lines.note: A cord is wound around this small wooden tool to tighten the garment very firmly. The final ve- begins veſtido on the following row, while q̃ remains unexpanded.

runs.text: ſtido, ou outra couſa que ſe ha de tingir.

lines.note: Completes veſtido and explains that the garment or other object is to be dyed. Tingir, with a worn descender, is supported by the cord-tightening context and visible type rather than OCR tincir.
Tegui, u, eida is a verb for reprimanding verbally or administering punishment. Its printed principal parts are retained rather than replaced with a guessed modern verb.
The second part of the gloss specifies punishment and blows given to someone. Pancadas and alguem each form single words; the OCR introduced spurious spaces.
Teguire is an uprising or rebellion. Aleuantamento and rebelião are supported by the visible letters, correcting OCR Aleuantamanto and re belião.
Teguire wo suru means carrying out such a rebellion. This illustrative verbal construction repeats the noun and confirms the reading of its worn type.
Teguireina characterizes something clean and polished or a well-finished work. The headword is worn at its start but repeated clearly in the next column’s garden example; limpa corrects OCR tim pa.
Completes the first column’s definition of Teguireina as a work finished to perfection. Teguireina niwa gives the clean-garden or courtyard example.

runs.text: Pateo limpo, ou bem varrido, & concertado.

lines.note: The niwa is a clean courtyard, well swept and put in order. Pateo and concertado correct the OCR’s damaged vowels and r/t confusion.

runs.text: Lustre, ou artificio dalgũa obra pri-

lines.note: Teguiua is the finish or workmanship of a piece, whether fine or the opposite. Artificio is the Portuguese term; its worn c has been restored from surviving ink and the word’s context.
Completes obra prima and introduces the contrasted forms tegiwa no yoi and warui. The Latin l separates good from bad workmanship, not two different objects.
Warui saiku completes the bad-workmanship alternative. The Portuguese contrasts obra prima with toſca, finely made with crude work.

Teguiuazauayacana describes a beautiful and polished thing. The Japanese compound belongs with the preceding workmanship vocabulary; its printed consonants are retained rather than normalized from a modern form.

runs.text: Peßoa de boas mãos, ou pera eſ-

lines.note: Teguiyôna describes someone with skilful hands. The damaged n in the adjectival ending is recovered in the headword; the gloss begins an example involving writing. The damaged ß in Peßoa matches the clear same-page sort in c1-l009; OCR Peſioa misread its broken right-hand component.

runs.text: creuer, ou pera algum officio de mãos, &c.

lines.note: Completes eſcreuer and broadens the skilled-hands description to any manual trade. Officio de mãos is a craft or manual occupation.
Tegome, ru, eta means seizing or restraining someone firmly. The Portuguese prẽ- begins the divided prendelo, with the nasal abbreviation retained.

runs.text: delo de maneira que ſe não bulla.

lines.note: Completes prendelo: hold the person so that he cannot move. This physical restraint is the verb’s given sense here.

runs.text: O afferrar dalguem, ou prendelo for-

lines.note: The noun Tegome names the act of gripping or holding someone tightly. The terminal for- is the beginning of fortemente on the next row.
Tegome ni suru repeats the act of firm restraint. Temente completes fortemente, and Idem sends back to that definition.
Tegorona, alternatively tegoro no, describes something easily handled. The gloss continues menea across the physical line break.

runs.text: nea. l, que ſe deixa tratar, & tomar com

lines.note: Completes menea and restates the meaning as allowing oneself to be handled and taken in the hands. The scan supports deixa and the visible ampersand omitted by OCR.
The object is proportionate to one’s hands and therefore manageable. Proporcionada is the visible Portuguese adjective, correcting OCR properdionada.
Tegorona catana, yari, teppô exemplifies manageable swords, spears, and guns. The first adjective repeats the headword and supports Te- rather than the OCR’s To-.

runs.text: Catana, lança, eſpingarda, &c. de bom ta-

lines.note: The Portuguese names sword, spear, and gun of a suitable size. Bom supplies the positive quality, correcting the OCR’s hom; ta- begins tamanho below.
Completes tamanho and adds that the weapon is manageable. Tegorona aite introduces a matching opponent rather than an object fitted to the hand.
The opponent is equivalent or proportionate in ability. The final word ends proporcionado before the rule; OCR added an unsupported final r.
A mim completes the comparison: an opponent matched to me. The short row closes this example before the next headword.
Tegotaye ga shita is the example for feeling a responsive impact. Sentir introduces the description of the sensation experienced in the hand.

runs.text: na mão que acerta no aluo, ou noutra couſa a

lines.note: The hand feels that the shot has struck the target or another object. This supplies the concrete impact sense of tegotaye.
Completes the shooting example with an arrow, ball, or similar projectile. Pilouro is retained as the historical Portuguese word for the shot or ball.
Tegouai describes firmness and severity in military discipline. The scan supports ſeuero, correcting the OCR’s vowel in ſeuaro.
The same firmness can apply in other matters, so the definition is not exclusively military. This continuation closes tegouai.

runs.text: Nome de hũa rede pequena de peſcar.

lines.note: Teguri names a small fishing net. The worn r in the headword and d in de are recovered from visible strokes; the next entry repeats the net name in a boat compound. The supplied NINJAL headword index also identifies Teguri after the independent scan reading.
Teguribune is a small boat associated with that net. The worn ſòmente means only, with its missing e recovered from the visible word and continuation.

runs.text: hùm, ou dous que puxão por eſta rede.

lines.note: Only one or two people fit in the boat, and they haul the net. Puxão corrects OCR purão. The weak mark in hùm is retained in the baseline grave form rather than changed to an expected nasal spelling.
Teguſocu covers little boxes and other equipment or accessories. The abraded initial is the capital T found in the surrounding headwords, not a lowercase r.
Brincos de molheres completes the description of women’s small accessories or ornaments. The noun is not narrowed to modern earrings by this gloss alone.

runs.text: Eſfregar as mãos tomando o cuſpo

lines.note: Teguſune is explained as rubbing the hands after taking saliva from the mouth. The u vowel fits both the visible type and the repeated example below, correcting OCR Teguſone.

runs.text: da boca como quando hum quer lutar, &c.

lines.note: The action is compared with preparing to wrestle. This continues the hand-rubbing explanation and does not introduce another headword.

Teguſune wo hiku names spitting into the hands and rubbing them in preparation. The repeated noun’s last vowel is worn; the e reading follows the headword and surviving type without treating the OCR’s a as certain.

runs.text: eſfregalas deſta maneira, ou molhando os dedos

lines.note: Completes the action as rubbing the hands in this fashion or moistening the fingers. Maneira is one word, with its worn r restored instead of the OCR’s internal space.
Na boca completes the alternative of wetting the fingers in the mouth. This closes the hand-preparation explanation before Tegicai.

runs.text: Couſa q̃ eſtà perto da mão, ou à mão.

lines.note: Tegicai denotes something close to the hand or ready at hand. The printed gi is retained as part of the historical romanization; eſtà corrects OCR eſà.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Couſa q̃ eſtà longe pera lhe apontar cõ

lines.note: The second gloss speaks of a distant object to be aimed at. Its apparently contrasting longe is clearly printed and retained rather than harmonized with the preceding perto.
O arco completes the reference to aiming with a bow. It belongs to the preceding qualification of Tegicai rather than beginning a separate definition.
Tei means manner, form, or mode. The compact Portuguese list gives closely related descriptions without selecting a modern Japanese character spelling.

runs.text: Teichǔ. i, Giqiniſoxôuo mǒſu. l, meya-

lines.note: Teichǔ is explained by directly making a petition or presenting a written memorial. The scan supports the missing i in Teichǔ and the long ſ in mǒſu; meya- begins the divided meyaſu below.
Meyaſu wo aguru completes the alternative expression for submitting a petition. Fazer petição and apreſenta- begin the Portuguese description across the next line break.

runs.text: la a algum ſenhor, eſperandoo no caminho cõ

lines.note: The petitioner presents the request to a lord by waiting for him along his route. ſenhor and eſperandoo restore letters lost by OCR without modernizing the doubled o.

runs.text: apetição, ou papel poſto em hum bambu aleuã-

lines.note: The petition or paper is placed on an elevated bamboo pole. The scan reads singular poſto before em, not the OCR’s added final s; aleuã- continues below.
Tado completes aleuantado. Teichǔ wo suru, alternatively moſu, gives the verbal construction for making this petition, and Fa- begins Fazer.
Completes Fazer ou apreſentar eſta petição: making or presenting this petition. This is the final physical row of the Teichǔ entry.

runs.text: Adu. Sem falta, ou certa, & de-

lines.note: Teido is an adverb meaning without fail, certainly, or decisively. Its damaged capital T replaces OCR r; de- begins determinadamente below.
Terminadamente completes the final adverbial gloss. This row is ordinary body text; the much lower signature and catchword are separate page furniture.

The far-right catchword is read Teifi.; the e and narrow i types are abraded, especially the final i whose dot is not secure. It is kept as a chosen nonblocking reading, distinct from the signature. The following page is not supplied in this package.
